Class NativeWifi

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.internal.NativeWifi
All Implemented Interfaces:
Wifi
public final class NativeWifi extends Object implements Wifi
The board's Wifi: each method is a Wi-Fi intrinsic the compiler lowers to the board's networking library, so it has no Java body and cannot run, or be mocked, on a desktop JVM. Mock Wifi instead.

    • begin

      public void begin(String ssid, String password)
      Description copied from interface: Wifi
      Starts station-mode Wi-Fi on UNO R4 WiFi. On UNO Q, Wi-Fi belongs to Linux and must already be configured through App Lab or nmcli; this method initializes the MCU-to-Linux bridge and ignores the credential arguments.
      Specified by:
      begin in interface Wifi

    • beginAP

      public void beginAP(String ssid, String password)
      Description copied from interface: Wifi
      Starts the board as a Wi-Fi access point named ssid, so a phone or laptop can join it directly (typically to serve a provisioning page through HttpServer). On UNO R4 WiFi, password is a WPA2 passphrase of at least 8 characters, or empty for an open network; call Wifi.localIP(int[]) after Wifi.status() reports Wifi.STATUS_AP_LISTENING to obtain the access point's address. On UNO Q the MCU cannot create an access point: Linux owns Wi-Fi, so the hotspot must already be running (nmcli device wifi hotspot ssid <ssid> password <password>); this method only initializes the MCU-to-Linux bridge, ignores both arguments, and Wifi.status() reports Wifi.STATUS_CONNECTED once the bridge is up.
      Specified by:
      beginAP in interface Wifi

    • localIP

      public void localIP(int[] octets)
      Description copied from interface: Wifi
      Writes the board's current IPv4 address into octets (caller-owned, at least 4 entries), one byte value (0-255) per element, most significant first — e.g. 192, 168, 1, 45. When Wifi.status() reports Wifi.STATUS_AP_LISTENING, this is the access point's address; when it reports Wifi.STATUS_CONNECTED, it is the station address. UNO Q's current router API does not expose either address and writes four zeroes. Juno has no heap, so there is no String-returning form here — print each octet with Serial.print(int) and a literal "." between them.
      Specified by:
      localIP in interface Wifi

    • gatewayIP

      public void gatewayIP(int[] octets)
      Description copied from interface: Wifi
      Writes the IPv4 address of the router the board is connected to (its gateway) into octets (at least 4 entries), in the same form as Wifi.localIP(int[]). Only meaningful once Wifi.status() reports Wifi.STATUS_CONNECTED; a gateway that does not share the board's subnet usually means a bad DHCP lease. UNO Q's router API does not expose it and writes four zeroes.
      Specified by:
      gatewayIP in interface Wifi

    • macAddress

      public void macAddress(int[] octets)
      Description copied from interface: Wifi
      Writes the Wi-Fi interface's six-byte hardware (MAC) address into octets (at least 6 entries), one byte value (0-255) per element, most significant first; print them in hex to compare against a router's client list. UNO Q's router API does not expose it and writes six zeroes.
      Specified by:
